chunks: From him, from Al-Hasan ibn Hisham, from Ya'qub ibn Shu'ayb, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about two men who have date palms between them, and one says to the other: 'Choose either that you take these date palms for such and such a specified measure, and give me half of that measure, whether it increases or decreases; or that I take them for that, and return [the value] to you.' He said, 'There is no objection to that.'

key_terms.زَادَ أَوْ نَقَصَ: Increased or decreased (referring to yield variation)
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِذَلِكَ: There is no objection to that (permissible)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on buying out a partner's share of date palms with a variable quantity payment?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) validates a flexible forward sale contract for date palms, addressing the practical uncertainty of agricultural yields. It permits co-owners to agree on a fixed quantity for one share while allowing the other share to vary with the actual harvest, thereby resolving disputes over fluctuating produce. This ruling highlights the Shia juristic emphasis on facilitating trade by accommodating natural variability in agricultural output.
